---
title: "Functions"
---

The polyfill implements 234 of phit 0.5.1's 235 functions. Signatures,
parameter names, defaults, and result keys are the extension's, so phit's
documentation describes each function's arguments and results.

| Area | Functions |
|---|---|
| Descriptive statistics | `stat_mean`, `stat_var`, `stat_sd`, `stat_median`, `stat_quantile`, `stat_quantile_array`, `stat_cov`, `stat_cor`, `stat_weighted_mean`, `stat_weighted_var` |
| Smoothing | `stat_density`, `stat_bw_nrd0`, `stat_bw_nrd`, `stat_approx`, `stat_ecdf` |
| Optimization | `optimize`, `uniroot` |
| Models from a formula | `fit_ols`, `fit_generalized_linear`, `fit_mixed_gaussian`, `fit_mixed_logistic`, `model_matrix`, `predict` |
| Models from a matrix | `fit_ols_matrix`, `fit_logistic_matrix`, `fit_probit_matrix`, `fit_poisson_matrix`, with weights, offsets, the automatic intercept, and both missing-value policies; `fit_mixed_gaussian_matrix`, `fit_mixed_gaussian_intercept_matrix`, `fit_mixed_logistic_matrix` |
| Fit objects and summaries | `summary`, `tidy`, the `Phit\Fit` interface and its four fit classes, and `Phit\Table` |
| Distributions | 13 families with 14 functions each, listed below |
| Random numbers | `dist_<family>_rng` for each of the 13 families, `dist_uniform_rng`, `dist_categorical_rng`, `dist_categorical_rows_rng`, `permutation_rng` |
| Posterior draws | `draws_moments`, `draws_covariance_map`, `draws_affine` |
| Extension only | `read_csv` and the `CsvReader` class |

All names are in the `Phit` namespace, for example `Phit\fit_ols`.

## Fit objects and summaries

Every model function returns a fit object. The class follows the result's
`model` key: `Phit\LinearFit`, `Phit\GeneralizedLinearFit`,
`Phit\MixedGaussianFit`, or `Phit\MixedLogisticFit`, each implementing the
interface `Phit\Fit`. A fit holds the result array and reads like it:
`$fit['coefficients']`, `isset()`, `count()`, `foreach`, and `json_encode()`
work as on the array, and nested values are plain arrays. Fits are read-only.
Writing a key throws `LogicException`, and `toArray()` returns an array copy.
Without the extension, the polyfill defines these classes with the
extension's names, methods, and messages.

`echo $fit` and `$fit->summary()` print the fit in the layout of R's
`print(summary(fit))`. The coefficient table follows
`printCoefmat(digits = 4)` without significance stars. `$fit->tidy()` and
`$fit->predict()` work as `tidy()` and `predict()`, and the free functions
`summary()`, `tidy()`, and `predict()` take a fit or an array in the same
shape.

`tidy()` returns a `Phit\Table` of columns named `term`, `estimate`,
`std_error`, `statistic`, and `p_value`. With `confInt`, it adds `conf_low`
and `conf_high`, which are Wald intervals at `level`. For mixed fits, `tidy()`
gives the fixed effects by default. With `effects: 'ran_vals'`, it gives each
group's conditional modes and their standard errors instead, in columns named
`group`, `level`, `term`, `estimate`, and `std_error`, as lme4's
`ranef(fit, condVar = TRUE)`. Their intervals use the normal distribution.
`echo $table` prints the columns in the layout of R's `print.data.frame()`,
and `$table->toColumns()` returns them as arrays.

```php
use function Phit\fit_ols;

$fit = fit_ols('mpg ~ wt + hp', $mtcars);
echo $fit;
echo $fit->tidy(confInt: true);
$columns = $fit->tidy()->toColumns();
```

The text is byte-identical to the extension's on phit's fixtures for mtcars,
mroz, MASS Insurance, sleepstudy, and cbpp, and the randomized parity suite
compares the summaries, the tables, and their printed text with the
extension on synthetic fits.

## CSV input

`Phit\read_csv` and the chunked reader `Phit\CsvReader` need the extension.
Without it they stay undefined, so `function_exists('Phit\read_csv')` and
`class_exists('Phit\CsvReader')` return `false`. phibble reads CSV files in
PHP when the extension is absent.

## Distributions

Each family has a density or mass function and its logarithm, `cdf`,
`logcdf`, `sf`, `logsf`, and `quantile`, each with an `_array` variant, and a
seeded sampler.

| Family | Prefix | Parameters |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | `dist_normal_` | mean, sd |
| Student's t | `dist_t_` | df |
| Chi-square | `dist_chisquare_` | df |
| F | `dist_f_` | df1, df2 |
| Exponential | `dist_exponential_` | rate |
| Logistic | `dist_logistic_` | location, scale |
| Log-normal | `dist_lognormal_` | meanlog, sdlog |
| Gamma | `dist_gamma_` | shape, scale |
| Beta | `dist_beta_` | alpha, beta |
| Binomial | `dist_binomial_` | size, prob |
| Poisson | `dist_poisson_` | lambda |
| Negative binomial | `dist_nbinom_` | size, prob |
| Negative binomial by mean | `dist_nbinom_mu_` | size, mu |

The continuous families use `pdf` and `logpdf`; the discrete families use
`pmf` and `logpmf`.

```php
use function Phit\{dist_t_sf, dist_normal_quantile_array, dist_normal_rng};

dist_t_sf(2.5, df: 12);
dist_normal_quantile_array([0.025, 0.975]);
dist_normal_rng(1000, seed: 42);
```

The samplers use the extension's generator: ChaCha20 seeded as in rand_core,
with inverse-CDF sampling. A seed gives the same draws, bit for bit, with or
without the extension. `dist_uniform_rng`, `dist_categorical_rng`,
`dist_categorical_rows_rng`, and `permutation_rng` take one uniform per draw
from the same stream.

## Formula interface

`model_matrix`, `fit_ols`, and `fit_generalized_linear` accept an R-style formula over named
columns. They follow the extension's parser, term expansion, and coding, so
column names, term order, contrasts, and missing-value handling match the
extension. Where the extension differs from R, the polyfill follows the
extension.

```php
use function Phit\{fit_ols, fit_generalized_linear, model_matrix, predict};

$data = [
    'rent' => [1879.25, 1805.03, 2022.29, 1267.85, 1509.24, 2240.10],
    'area' => [74.4, 57.4, 66.4, 49.1, 45.7, 92.4],
    'district' => ['north', 'south', 'north', 'east', 'east', 'south'],
];

$fit = fit_ols('rent ~ log(area) + district', $data);
$fit['named'];    // coefficients keyed by column name

$design = model_matrix('~ area * district', $data);
$design['columns'];

$new = predict($fit, ['area' => [60.0, 80.0], 'district' => ['east', 'north']],
    interval: 'prediction');
```

Supported syntax includes `+ - : * / %in% ^`, `0`/`1`/`-1`, `.`, `offset()`,
`I()`, the common transforms (`log`, `log2`, `log10`, `log1p`, `exp`, `sqrt`,
`abs`, and others), `poly()`, `factor()`, `ordered()`, and `cbind()` responses
for grouped binomial data. Families are gaussian, binomial (logit or probit),
and poisson. Random-effect bars such as `(1 | g)` are accepted by
`model_matrix`, which returns the random-effect design, and are fitted by
`fit_mixed_gaussian` and `fit_mixed_logistic`. `fit_ols` and `fit_generalized_linear` reject them with code 1007.

## Mixed models

The five mixed-model functions follow the extension's code and support the
same structures:

- `fit_mixed_gaussian_intercept_matrix` fits a linear model with one random intercept.
- `fit_mixed_gaussian_matrix` and `fit_mixed_gaussian` fit linear mixed models by REML (the default) or
  maximum likelihood, with the BOBYQA (default) or Nelder–Mead optimizer.
  `fit_mixed_gaussian` accepts random intercepts and slopes, correlated `(x | g)` and
  uncorrelated `(x || g)` terms, several terms such as
  `(x | subject) + (1 | item)`, and nested groups such as `(1 | subject/item)`.
- `fit_mixed_logistic_matrix` and `fit_mixed_logistic` fit a binomial logit model with one
  random intercept, `(1 | g)`, by the Laplace approximation (the default) or
  adaptive Gauss–Hermite quadrature with 2 to 61 points. `fit_mixed_logistic`
  takes no `family` or `link` argument, and it rejects random slopes and more
  than one term with code 1007.

The lme4 reference fixtures cover each of these structures, and the polyfill
agrees with them within the extension's tolerances. The randomized parity
suite compares random-intercept and random-slope fits with the extension and
finds them identical to the bit.

## Posterior draws

`draws_moments`, `draws_covariance_map`, and `draws_affine` summarize and
transform matrices of posterior draws. They follow the extension's operation
order, including the fused multiply-adds of its matrix products, so their
results match the extension's to the bit.

## Warnings and exceptions

When rows with missing values are dropped, the fitting functions warn with
`E_USER_WARNING`, for example `Phit\fit_logistic_matrix(): dropped 2 of 80
observations with missing values (listwise deletion)`. The
extension raises the same text as `E_WARNING`.

Exceptions are plain `\Exception` instances whose code identifies the
category, as in the extension.

| Code | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 1001 | Invalid input |
| 1002 | Dimension mismatch |
| 1003 | Non-finite value or overflow |
| 1004 | Rank deficiency |
| 1005 | Factorization failure |
| 1006 | Non-convergence (including separation) |
| 1007 | Unsupported input size |
| 1008 | Internal error |
